extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent prosecutors, and applicants seeking to use 37 CFR 1.130 or invoke AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) exceptions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on using affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 to disqualify disclosures as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) and (2), and on invoking the commonly‑owned/joint research agreement exception under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) grace-period exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure made one year or less before the effective filing date of a claimed invention shall not be prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) if: (1) the disclosure was made by the inventor or joint inventor or by another who obtained the subject matter disclosed directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor; or (2) the subject matter disclosed had, before such disclosure, been publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor or by another who obtained the subject matter disclosed directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office treats the term 'disclosure' broadly to encompass the documents and activities enumerated in 35 U.S.C. 102(a) (patented, printed publication, public use, on sale, otherwise available to the public). See MPEP § 2153 et seq. for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A)/(B) exception for 102(a)(2) disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure shall not be prior art to a claimed invention under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if: (1) the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor; or (2) the subject matter disclosed had, before such subject matter was effectively filed, been publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor or another who obtained the subject matter disclosed directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception applies to subject matter that appears in patents or published patent applications (102(a)(2)). See MPEP § 2154.02 et seq. for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) common ownership/assignment exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure made in a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO published application shall not be prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if, not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention, the subject matter disclosed and the claimed invention were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision replaces pre‑AIA 103(c) and means certain patents and published applications of coworkers/collaborators may not be prior art for novelty (102) or nonobviousness (103). See MPEP § 717.02 et seq. and the CREATE Act / joint research agreement rules under 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) and 1.104(c)(4)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism to invoke exceptions: 37 CFR 1.130
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.130 provides a mechanism for filing an affidavit or declaration to establish that a disclosure is not prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) due to an exception in 35 U.S.C. 102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132, 37 CFR 1.130 is a mechanism to submit evidence to disqualify a disclosure as prior art or otherwise traverse a rejection. Compliance entitles the evidence to be considered but does not guarantee withdrawal of the rejection as a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.130(a) – affidavit/declaration of attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: When any claim is rejected, the applicant or patent owner may submit an affidavit or declaration to disqualify a disclosure as prior art by establishing that the disclosure was made by the inventor or a joint inventor, or that the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.130(a) pertains to subparagraph (A) of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) and 102(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.130(b) – affidavit/declaration of prior public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When any claim is rejected, an applicant or patent owner may submit an affidavit or declaration to disqualify a disclosure as prior art by establishing that the subject matter disclosed had, before such disclosure was made or before such subject matter was effectively filed, been publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor or another who obtained the subject matter disclosed directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit/declaration must identify the subject matter publicly disclosed and provide the date such subject matter was publicly disclosed. If the prior disclosure was in a printed publication, a copy must accompany the affidavit (37 CFR 1.130(b)(1)). If not in a printed publication, the affidavit must describe the subject matter with sufficient detail and particularity to determine what was publicly disclosed (37 CFR 1.130(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limitation: 37 CFR 1.130(c) – one-year grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 37 CFR 1.130 are not available if the rejection is based upon a disclosure made more than one year before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclosure made more than one year before the effective filing date is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) and cannot be excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1). Note: 1.130 may still be relevant for certain 102(a)(2) situations described at MPEP § 2155.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of applications/patents to which 37 CFR 1.130 applies
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions apply to any application for patent, and to any patent issuing thereon, that contains (or contained) a claim with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013; or which contains a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) to any patent or application that contains (or contained) such a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In short, 1.130 applies to AIA (first‑inventor‑to‑file) applications as defined in the MPEP and 35 U.S.C. 100 (note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 37 CFR 1.130 may be used (general examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 may be used to show a disclosure (or portion thereof) applied in a 102(a)(1) or 102(a)(2) rejection is eligible to be excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) or (2) by establishing the disclosure was made by the inventor/joint inventor, was obtained from them, or had been publicly disclosed by them prior to the intervening disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If effective, the showing will make the disclosure unavailable for use in rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 35 U.S.C. 103 (e.g., to defeat an obviousness rejection that relies on that disclosure as one element). However, such references can still be used for other purposes (e.g., evidence of level of ordinary skill, enablement inquiry, or double patenting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 37 CFR 1.130 is inappropriate (derivation/patent document with same invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 is not appropriate when the disclosure applied in a rejection is a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that (a) claims an invention that is the same or substantially the same as the applicant’s claimed invention, and (b) the affidavit or declaration contends that an inventor named in that patent/publication derived the claimed invention from the inventor named in the application under examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such a case, the applicant or patent owner may file a petition for a derivation proceeding under 37 CFR 42.401 et seq. However, 1.130 can still be available if: (1) the rejection is based on a disclosure other than a U.S. patent/publication (e.g., non‑patent literature or foreign patent); (2) the patent/publication did not claim the same or substantially the same invention; or (3) the 1.130 submission does not allege derivation but instead relies on prior public disclosure by the inventor or an originator.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.130 not available if disclosure >1 year before effective filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the rejection is based upon a disclosure made more than one year before the effective filing date of the claimed invention, 37 CFR 1.130 cannot be used to except that disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule is restated multiple times and cross‑references MPEP § 2152.01 for determining effective filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a 1.130(a) declaration is not required (inventive entity overlap)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(a) is not required when a public disclosure, subject to the exceptions of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A), is by one or more joint inventor(s) or the entire inventive entity of the application under examination and does not name anyone else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: If the application names A, B, and C as the inventive entity and a publication names A and B as authors (publication date within one year), the publication should not be applied in a prior art rejection because it appears to be a grace period disclosure. Similarly for patent documents that name only joint inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a 1.130(a) declaration is not required (patent/publication names subset of inventive entity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(a) is not required when the inventive entity of a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO publication, subject to the exceptions of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A), only includes one or more joint inventor(s), but not the entire inventive entity, of the application under examination and does not name anyone else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: application inventive entity A, B, C; 102(a)(2) reference names A and B — the reference should not be applied in a 102(a)(2) rejection because it appears that the subject matter was obtained from one or more members of the inventive entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a 1.130(a) declaration is not required (specification identifies origin)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(a) is not required if the specification of the application under examination identifies the disclosure or the subject matter disclosed that is subject to the exceptions of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A) or 102(b)(2)(A) as having been made by or having originated from one or more members of the inventive entity of the application under examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.77(b)(6) and MPEP § 2153.01(a) for further guidance on specification statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria for 37 CFR 1.130(a) submissions (weight and character of facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating whether a declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(a) is effective, Office personnel will consider whether the affidavit shows sufficient facts, in weight and character, to establish that (1) the disclosure was made by the inventor or a joint inventor, or (2) the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include authorship (presence of inventor among authors), an 'unequivocal' statement from the inventor/joint inventor that he/she (or a specific combination) invented the subject matter accompanied by a reasonable explanation for additional authors, and consideration of evidence to the contrary (see In re DeBaun). Corroborating documentary evidence and reasonable explanations increase weight; lack of corroboration or evidence to the contrary reduces effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria for 37 CFR 1.130(b) submissions (identifying prior public disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1.130(b), the affidavit or declaration must identify the subject matter publicly disclosed and the date of public disclosure; if the prior disclosure was a printed publication a copy must be provided, otherwise the submission must describe the subject matter with sufficient detail and particularity to determine what was publicly disclosed on that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office personnel will assess whether the description and evidence are sufficiently specific and probative to show the claimed subject matter was publicly disclosed by the inventor/joint inventor prior to the intervening disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements and who may make affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 must meet formal requirements and be made by an appropriate person (e.g., the inventor or a person with knowledge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 717.01(c) and related MPEP sections for detailed formalities (signatures, witness/oath where required, proper identification of subject matter and dates). The Office treats 1.130 submissions analogously to 1.131/1.132 submissions in terms of formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / seasonable presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 must be seasonably (timely) presented to be entitled to consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 717.01(e)/(f) for details; late or untimely submissions may be given less weight or treated under petition practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of successful 1.130 showing on rejections and other uses of references
rubrics_metrics.description: If effective, the showing that a disclosure is not prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) will make that disclosure unavailable to be applied in a rejection under either 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the U.S. patents or published applications may still be applied under doctrines of nonstatutory/statutory double patenting or used as evidence of level of ordinary skill, enablement, or other issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph use and required content when 1.130 is effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.67.aia when an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 is sufficient to overcome the rejection; the paragraph includes brackets to identify whether affidavit or declaration, subsection (a) or (b), filing date, affected claims, the specific reference disqualified, and an explanation of how the submission provides evidence of reliance on an exception in 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) or (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes specify that form paragraph 7.67.aia should be used only for applications filed on or after March 16, 2013, examined under AIA 102/103, and must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph use and required content when 1.130 is ineffective
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.68.aia when an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 is insufficient to overcome the rejection; brackets identify affidavit/declaration, subsection, filing date, affected claims, the rejection not overcome, and an explanation why the submission fails to provide evidence of reliance on exception provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same examiner-note restrictions apply: AIA applications only; preceded by 7.03.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invoking 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) (common ownership / joint research agreement) – statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To except subject matter in a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C), an applicant must provide a proper statement indicating common ownership or obligation to assign not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention, or comply with CREATE Act / joint research agreement requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to provide required statements or required specification amendments (e.g., naming parties to the joint research agreement), the attempt to invoke 102(b)(2)(C) is ineffective and form paragraph 7.20.05.aia should be used to inform applicant what is missing. The applicant may alternatively rely on 37 CFR 1.130(a) or 1.130(b) showings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when 102(b)(2)(C) invocation is attempted but ineffective
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an attempt has been made to except subject matter under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) but the attempt is ineffective (e.g., missing statement, failure to amend specification), the examiner should include specific form paragraphs identifying the commonly owned applied art and the common assignee, and explain the deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See form paragraph 7.20.05.aia and instructions about when to use 7.38.01 or 7.38.02 where submission is persuasive; see MPEP § 707.07(f) for additional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references for determining prior art dates and related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of prior art dates for disclosures under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) and 102(a)(2) should follow MPEP § 2152.02(a) et seq. and MPEP § 2154.01 et seq., respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other related sections include MPEP § 2153 (102(b)(1) exceptions), § 2154.02 (102(b)(2) exceptions), § 2155.06 (special 102(a)(2) timing situations), and sections on affidavits under 1.131/1.132 for pre‑AIA practice (e.g., MPEP §§ 715, 716).
